messages:
josh: Thanks for the all-hands walkthrough. Two quick clarifications on the new SKU/credit model: 1) if we switch model variants mid-request (fallback), which SKU is charged? 2) are per-route quotas shared across projects in the same org?
sara (ceo): Great questions. 1) charge is based on the model actually used to produce tokens. 2) quotas are scoped to the org by default but can be set at project or route level.
nina (product): Adding detail: fallback routing happens after token estimation; if we start on a high-capacity model and failover to a smaller variant mid-stream, billing will reflect the final emitted tokens on the fallback model. We surface both model-labeled usage lines in Console.
harry (finance): Also worth calling out: we provide an hourly aggregated export with per-model, per-route breakdown for reconciliation.
josh: If quotas are org-scoped, how do we avoid noisy neighbours across product teams?
mina (eng): Ops patterns: 1) create separate projects for teams that need isolation, 2) attach route-level quotas and priority labels, 3) enable prefilling of KV caches for latency-critical routes. Priority labels influence fairshare but not billing.
rachel (support): For support: standard onboarding checklist suggests creating a dev project with tiny credit bucket + alerts to avoid surprise spend. We can also add a readonly billing view for PMs.
josh: Any automatic refund or reversal if the system misroutes and uses a more expensive model?
sara (ceo): We don’t auto-refund for routing optimizations. If a system error resulted in incorrect billing, support will investigate and apply credits if warranted. Follow the incident appeal flow.
billing-bot: billing: per-route metering endpoint v1.2 deployed 2025-02-11T14:03:22Z
nina (product): Roadmap note: Console will show projected spend per active route for the next billing period (beta) 125.
harry (finance): For enterprise customers we can map SKUs to internal GL codes via the billing export. Ask your account manager.
josh: Last: can we set hard stops (deny traffic) when credit buckets drain?
mina (eng): Yes, two options: soft (alerts + throttling) or hard (deny responses with 402). Hard stops require an org-level flag.
rachel (support): If you want us to enable hard stops on a trial org, file a support ticket and include your org id and desired behavior.
josh: Perfect, thanks. Will follow up for a policy doc and sample configs. :thumbsup:
